name: Texas Data Privacy and Security Act
version: Business and Commerce Code as published November 2026
full_name: Texas Data Privacy and Security Act (Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 541)
issuing_body: State of Texas; published by the Texas Legislative Council
aliases: Texas Data Privacy and Security Act
notice: Assessed against Chapter 541 of the Texas Business and Commerce Code as published by the Texas Legislative Council in November 2026.

sources.title: Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 541, Consumer Data Protection (chapter page)

control_flags.objectives: The numbered items of a subsection; each is required, or each prohibited under "may not", unless the lead-in makes them a choice.

scoring.summary: Percentage of applicable requirements that are implemented. The Act defines no score; this percentage is an HCG measure of progress.

rules.summary: A requirement is met only when every element it lists is met.

The Act applies to a person that does business in Texas or offers products or services consumed there, processes or sells personal data, and is not a small business as the U.S. Small Business Administration defines it; small businesses remain bound by section 541.107 on selling sensitive data.
rules.quote: is not a small business as defined by the United States Small Business Administration

rules.summary: A consumer request is answered without undue delay and within 45 days of receipt; the period may be extended once by 45 days.
rules.quote: which may not be later than the 45th day after the date of receipt of the request.

rules.summary: An appeal is decided and answered in writing within 60 days of receipt.
rules.quote: not later than the 60th day after the date of receipt of the appeal

rules.summary: Before suing, the attorney general gives written notice; a violation cured within 30 days, with a written statement, is not pursued.
rules.quote: within the 30-day period, the person cures the identified violation

consequences.summary: A violation that continues after the cure period carries a civil penalty of up to $7,500 for each violation, recoverable by the attorney general with injunctive relief.
consequences.quote: is liable for a civil penalty in an amount not to exceed $7,500 for each violation.

glossary.definition: The Texas Data Privacy and Security Act, Texas's comprehensive consumer privacy law, in force since 1 July 2024.
The person that, alone or jointly with others, determines the purpose and means of processing personal data.
A person that processes personal data on behalf of a controller.

Personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, religious beliefs, health diagnosis, sexual orientation, citizenship or immigration status; genetic or biometric data used to identify a person; data of a known child; and precise geolocation data.

A documented assessment, required before targeted advertising, sale of personal data, certain profiling and processing of sensitive data, that weighs the benefits of processing against the risks to consumers.
